name: Cielo
why_it_matters: Largest acquirer by merchant base: UBS BB survey for January 2026 gives Cielo 28% of card-machine users and 17% of transacted volume (tied with PagBank, behind Rede's 18%).

name: Rede
why_it_matters: Itaú's acquirer became volume leader in January 2026 with 18% of transacted volume and 25% of users (+5 pp YoY) per UBS BB; bundled with Itaú accounts and credit.

name: Stone
why_it_matters: Independent acquirer with 15% of transacted volume and 22% of users in January 2026 (UBS BB), both down 2 pp YoY; SMB-weighted but a full local acquiring option.

name: Getnet
why_it_matters: Santander's acquirer held 5% of transacted volume and 9% of users in January 2026 (UBS BB); enterprise-oriented and part of Santander's PagoNxt network across LatAm.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Wallet-as-acquirer and checkout: Mercado Pago reported 88 million monthly active users (+30% YoY) and USD 101.0 billion TPV in Q2 2026, with Brazil named as the strongest MAU growth market.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Global PSP offering Pix (listed as available in Brazil, 'built and owned by Brazil's Central Bank', 700+ institutions) and Boleto; Adyen's global-processing page lists Brazil among full Adyen Acquiring markets.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator whose Brazil docs cover Visa/MC/Amex/Elo/Hipercard/Discover cards, Pix (incl. Pix Automático and Open Finance), Boleto, Mercado Pago, PicPay, NuPay and Pagaleve BNPL.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: Brazil-born cross-border PSP; its Pix page claims direct participation in the Pix system and recognition by the Central Bank of Brazil for Pix processing; also offers Boleto, Mercado Pago, PicPay, NuPay and Pagaleve.

name: Pix
why_it_matters: Pix is the #1 online method: 42% of Brazilian e-commerce transaction value in 2025 (Worldpay Global Payments Report 2026, 2030 projection 44%); the Central Bank counted 148 million individuals using Pix and close to 80 billion transactions in 2025.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Credit cards were 40% and debit 4% of e-commerce value in 2025 (Worldpay GPR 2026); Adyen's LatAm guide states 80% of Brazil's e-commerce payments are made in installments, so parcelamento support is mandatory; local schemes Elo and Hipercard are 13% of card spend (PPRO).
typical_access: direct via local acquirer, or via dLocal, EBANX, Adyen

name: Elo
why_it_matters: Domestic scheme launched 2011 by Banco do Brasil, Bradesco and Caixa: 34 million active cards and R$310.9 billion transacted in 2025 (37 issuers); not accepted on most cross-border acquiring, so it needs a local connection.
typical_access: direct via local acquirer, or via dLocal

name: Boleto
why_it_matters: Barcode voucher payable in cash or via bank apps; EBANX puts Boleto at nearly USD 27 billion and 8% of Brazil's online sales volume in 2024, while PPRO shows cash (incl. Boleto) at 3% of e-commerce; declining but still expected at checkout.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Digital wallets were 10% of e-commerce value in 2025 (Worldpay GPR 2026, projected 15% by 2030); Mercado Pago is the largest with 88 million MAU group-wide in Q2 2026. Checkout Pro (one-shot) and Wallet Connect (tokenized) flows.

name: PicPay
why_it_matters: Brazilian digital wallet offered as a redirect method by dLocal and EBANX; no public e-commerce share figure found for PicPay alone (wallets in total are 10% of e-commerce per Worldpay 2026).

name: NuPay
why_it_matters: Nubank's in-app payment method (tokenized, supports recurring) available through dLocal and EBANX; no public share figure found for NuPay alone.

name: Pagaleve
why_it_matters: Pix-based BNPL ('Pix 4x', 40 to 8,000 BRL, fortnightly interest-free plan) available via dLocal and EBANX; BNPL overall is only 1% of Brazilian e-commerce (PPRO), so relevance is incremental to card installments.

name: Adyen
why_it_matters: Adyen activated full (local) acquiring in Mexico in 2022 alongside its unified-commerce launch, and offers OXXO ('the largest alternative payment method in Mexico', 18,000+ stores).

name: Conekta
why_it_matters: Mexican gateway with 14 years in market: +8K merchants, +428M transactions and USD 15B processed; offers cards (Visa/MC/Amex), SPEI, cash (Conekta Efectivo), Apple/Google Pay and BNPL (Aplazo, Creditea).

name: Openpay
why_it_matters: BBVA-owned gateway: transaction volume above MXN 503 billion (MXN 107 billion through the online payment gateway), 142+ million annual transactions (+80% YoY) and a Paynet cash network of 20,000+ points (BBVA, Sept 2026).

name: Getnet
why_it_matters: Santander's acquirer; at April 2021 it was second in merchants served with about 17% of the market, almost 160,000 active POS terminals and 390 million transactions in 12 months. No newer public share figure found.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Wallet-as-acquirer and checkout; Mercado Pago reported 88 million MAU in Q2 2026 with Mexico named alongside Brazil for standout user growth. Checkout Pro and Wallet Connect are exposed through dLocal and EBANX.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator covering Visa/MC/Amex/Carnet cards, OXXO, SPEI, CoDi, Mercado Pago (Wallet Connect and Checkout Pro), Mercado Crédito, Kueski Pay and DiDi BNPL, and bank direct debit in Mexico.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP listing OXXO Pay, Paynet, Mercado Pago, Mercado Pago Credit and Aplazo for Mexico, plus SPEI on its instant-payments page.

name: PayU (Rapyd)
why_it_matters: PayU Latam is now part of Rapyd (acquisition completed March 2025; card acquiring in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Peru); Mexico docs cover Visa/MC cards, OXXO and 7-Eleven cash, Google Pay and bank-specific installments (MSI).

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards are 56% of Mexican e-commerce (PPRO): Visa 60%, Mastercard 35%, Amex 3%, Carnet and other 2%. 'Meses sin intereses' bank-promoted installments are standard (PayU docs expose INSTALLMENTS_NUMBER per bank for Mexico).
typical_access: direct via local acquirer, or via dLocal, EBANX, Adyen, PayU

name: OXXO Pay
why_it_matters: Cash voucher paid at 20,000+ OXXO stores (EBANX); PPRO states OXXO Pay is used for nearly 20% of online payments while its 'cash incl. OXXO' category is 8% of e-commerce. Cash-based payments reached USD 6.1B in 2024 (EBANX).

name: SPEI
why_it_matters: Banxico's real-time transfer system: over 6 billion operations in 2025, about 16x GDP (Mobile Time citing Banxico); bank transfer is 7% of e-commerce (PPRO) and growing. CoDi and DiMo run on top of SPEI.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: E-wallets are 28% of Mexican e-commerce (PPRO), the second-largest category after cards; Mercado Pago is the main local wallet (88 million MAU group-wide, Q2 2026).

name: Kueski Pay
why_it_matters: Leading Mexican BNPL: offered by 33% of top e-commerce merchants (Oct 2025), 3 million BNPL payments on Amazon by Aug 2025, ~250,000 new users per month, average ticket MXN 2,500; integrated with dLocal for international merchants. BNPL is ~1-2% of e-commerce.

name: Aplazo
why_it_matters: Second BNPL player: online exclusivity with Walmart (1.5 million pre-approved credits), 771 Soriana stores, BBVA Spark credit line raised to USD 50 million; available through EBANX and Conekta. No public user count found.

name: CoDi
why_it_matters: Banxico's QR/push request-to-pay on SPEI; dLocal exposes CoDi QR and push. Adoption is limited (1.6 million accounts registered in 2020, minimal operations) while sister scheme DiMo had 12+ million linked accounts by late 2024.

name: Redeban
why_it_matters: Card processor/acquirer network: 2,086 million of the industry's 4,055 million monetary transactions in 2024 (51% share), with 60% of the card rail; also a Bre-B node.

name: Credibanco
why_it_matters: Second card acquirer/processor: 361+ million transactions to April 2025 and 304,000+ access points; the only processor managing Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Diners and UPI; an enabler of Bre-B interoperability.

name: Wompi
why_it_matters: Bancolombia's gateway: about COP 25 trillion and ~70 million transactions in 2024 (TPV doubled), 55,000 merchants by 2026; native access to Bancolombia Button and Nequi.

name: PayU (Rapyd)
why_it_matters: Historic leading gateway in Colombia, now part of Rapyd (acquisition completed March 2025 with card acquiring in Colombia); its Colombia docs cover cards, PSE, Nequi, Bancolombia Button, Bre-B QR, Google Pay and cash/bank reference.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Mercado Pago Checkout Pro and Wallet Connect are offered in Colombia (listed on dLocal's Colombia page); no public Colombia-specific share figure found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator covering Visa/MC/Amex/Diners/Codensa cards, PSE, Nequi (push, QR, mixed), Bre-B (QR and biometrics), Efecty, Bancolombia cash, Mercado Pago and Addi BNPL in Colombia.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP listing Nequi and Efecty for Colombia on its APM page and PSE on its instant-payments page; claims 100+ direct connections with local acquirers.

name: PSE
why_it_matters: ACH Colombia's online bank-debit button: bank transfer is 29% of e-commerce (PPRO); PSE processed 487+ million transactions in H1 2026 with 35,000+ companies connected and is cited as six of every ten Colombian digital payments.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards are 36% of e-commerce (PPRO): Mastercard 56%, Visa 42%, Amex 1%; Diners and the Codensa store card matter locally (dLocal). Installments are selected at checkout by the cardholder's bank.
typical_access: direct via Redeban/Credibanco, or via dLocal, EBANX, PayU

name: Nequi
why_it_matters: Bancolombia-origin wallet with 28 million active users at its 10th anniversary (May 2026); e-wallets are 26% of Colombian e-commerce (PPRO). Push, QR and tokenized flows.

name: Bre-B
why_it_matters: Banco de la República's instant payment system launched 2025: 116 million keys, 36 million linked clients and over COP 262 trillion moved in its first year (Oct 2026). Merchant QR and biometric flows are already exposed by dLocal and PayU.

name: Efecty
why_it_matters: Main cash-voucher network: cash is 8% of Colombian e-commerce (PPRO) and EBANX reports Efecty growing 17% yearly since 2020. No public point-count figure found on an opened page.

name: Addi
why_it_matters: Leading Colombian BNPL: 2.7 million active consumers, 33,000 merchants, 1,034 municipalities (Jan 2026); 47% of users have no credit card. BNPL is still ~1% of e-commerce (PPRO).

name: Bancolombia Button
why_it_matters: Direct debit from Bancolombia accounts (the largest bank), offered by PayU as 'Bancolombia Button' and natively by Wompi; no public share figure found.

name: Transbank
why_it_matters: Incumbent acquirer and operator of Webpay: FNE data put Transbank at 40-50% of non-presencial (e-commerce) acquiring by transactions in 2025, down from 60-70% in 2023; 40-50% of in-person acquiring in 2025.

name: Kushki
why_it_matters: Non-bank regional acquirer ('el adquirente regional no bancario de LATAM') with a Chilean operating entity; FNE data give Kushki 20-30% of non-presencial acquiring in 2025, up from 0-5% in 2023.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Wallet-as-acquirer: 20-30% of non-presencial acquiring in each of 2023-2025 and 10-20% of in-person acquiring in 2025 (FNE).

name: Getnet
why_it_matters: Santander's acquiring network, live since 1 March 2021 (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Magna); 20-30% of in-person acquiring in 2025 per FNE, no reported non-presencial share.

name: Klap
why_it_matters: Acquirer (ex-Multicaja) with 0-5% of both presencial and non-presencial acquiring in 2024-2025 (FNE); Itaú Chile's purchase was approved by the FNE.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator covering Visa/MC/Amex/CMR cards, MACH prepaid, Webpay, Khipu, high-ticket transfers via Fintoc, Servipag and Sencillito cash, and Mercado Pago in Chile.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP listing Mercado Pago, MACH, Servipag and Sencillito for Chile; Servipag is also on its instant-payments page.

name: PayU (Rapyd)
why_it_matters: Part of Rapyd since March 2025 (card acquiring in Chile); Chile docs cover cards, Khipu bank transfer and Webpay Plus debit/prepaid (TRANSBANK_DEBIT).

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards are 53% of Chilean e-commerce (PPRO) and local schemes (retailer cards such as CMR Falabella) are 44% of card spend, Visa 30%, Mastercard 26%; Redcompra debit runs through Webpay. Installment ('cuotas') support is expected.
typical_access: direct via Transbank/Getnet/Kushki, or via dLocal, EBANX, PayU

name: Webpay
why_it_matters: Transbank's gateway ('Webpay es la pasarela de pago de Transbank'): Webpay Plus for credit, Redcompra debit and prepaid cards, OneClick for tokenized one-click; the default checkout experience Chilean shoppers expect.

name: Khipu
why_it_matters: Bank-transfer payments 'sin tarjetas ni redirecciones' from any bank, prepaid or wallet: 4,000+ merchants and USD 300M+ per month collected; bank transfer is 21% of Chilean e-commerce (PPRO).

name: MACH
why_it_matters: Bci's digital account/prepaid wallet with 4.2 million users (Oct 2024); e-wallets are 22% of Chilean e-commerce (PPRO). Accepted as a prepaid card via dLocal and as MACH Pay via EBANX.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Mercado Pago wallet (Checkout Pro and Wallet Connect) in Chile; together with its 20-30% non-presencial acquiring share (FNE) it is the main wallet at Chilean checkouts; no wallet-only share figure found.

name: Servipag
why_it_matters: Cash/bill-payment network: EBANX reports 16% of Chile's population as users in 2022; cash is only 3% of Chilean e-commerce (PPRO). Sencillito is the alternative cash network.

name: Fintoc
why_it_matters: Account-to-account payments platform used by 1,200+ companies; powers dLocal's 'High-Ticket Bank Transfer' in Chile. No public share figure found.

name: Niubiz
why_it_matters: Market-leading acquirer (ex-VisaNet Perú): about S/ 75,000 million processed in 632 million transactions in 2024 (+25% in count); also reports 1,300 million Yape/Plin interoperability transactions worth S/ 87,500 million.

name: Izipay
why_it_matters: Intercorp/Interbank acquirer with 1.2 million merchant clients; its CEO estimated a market share above 45% in 2024 (self-reported).

name: Culqi
why_it_matters: BCP/Credicorp payment platform that began operating as an independent acquirer in 2024; accepts Visa, MC, Diners, Amex, Yape, Plin, Apple/Google Pay, PagoEfectivo and 'cuotas sin intereses'. No public volume figure found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator covering Visa/MC/Amex/Diners cards, Yape (one-shot and recurring), PagoEfectivo cash, BCP bank transfer, Payvalida and LigoPay QR (works with Plin) in Peru.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP listing PagoEfectivo and SafetyPay for Peru; reports APMs at 37% and cash-based methods at 19% of Peruvian e-commerce (2022).

name: PayU (Rapyd)
why_it_matters: Part of Rapyd since March 2025 (card acquiring in Peru); Peru docs cover cards, Yape ('mobile digital wallet from BCP') and PagoEfectivo cash.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards are 52% of Peruvian e-commerce with Visa at 81% of card spend, Mastercard 17% (PPRO); Diners Club is accepted locally (dLocal). Almost 50% of online transactions use something other than a card.
typical_access: direct via Niubiz/Izipay/Culqi, or via dLocal, EBANX, PayU

name: Yape
why_it_matters: BCP's wallet with 15.9 million monthly active users and 9.8 million daily transacting users (April 2026); e-wallets are 11% of e-commerce (PPRO, 2024) and growing. Interoperable with Plin since 2023.

name: Plin
why_it_matters: Interbank/BBVA/Scotiabank wallet interoperable with Yape (free transfers since April 2023); the Yape-Plin network handled 1,300 million transactions in 2024 (Niubiz). No public Plin-only share figure found; accepted via Culqi and dLocal's LigoPay QR.

name: PagoEfectivo
why_it_matters: CIP-code method paid in cash at thousands of agents or via mobile banking and wallets; EBANX reports 18% of total payments share (2022) and PPRO shows cash at 10% of e-commerce.

name: Bank transfer (BCP)
why_it_matters: Bank transfer is 17% of Peruvian e-commerce (PPRO); dLocal exposes BCP bank transfer and Payvalida redirect transfers. No single-rail share figure found.

name: Payway
why_it_matters: Advent-owned acquirer (formerly Prisma's acquiring arm) that 'continuará operando de manera independiente en el negocio de adquirencia' after Visa bought Prisma and Newpay (Feb 2026).

name: Fiserv
why_it_matters: PosNet/Clover acquirer with almost 400,000 active terminals nationwide and acceptance of 160+ brands; ePosNet and Link de pagos for e-commerce.

name: Prisma
why_it_matters: Card processor for credit, debit and prepaid issuers, acquired by Visa together with Newpay (Banelco, PagoMisCuentas) in 2026; relevant as issuer-side processor rather than acquirer.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Wallet-as-acquirer and checkout in its home market; 88 million MAU group-wide in Q2 2026 and credit-card rollout in Argentina. E-wallets are 34% of Argentine e-commerce (PPRO).

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Cross-border aggregator covering Visa/MC/Amex plus local cards (Cabal, Naranja, Argencard, Nativa, Cencosud, CMR), bank transfer, interoperable QR, MODO, Rapipago, Pago Fácil and Pareto BNPL in Argentina.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: Cross-border PSP listing Mercado Pago, Mercado Pago Credit, Rapipago and Pago Fácil for Argentina, and Debin bank transfer on its instant-payments page.

name: PayU (Rapyd)
why_it_matters: Part of Rapyd since March 2025 (card acquiring in Argentina); Argentina docs cover cards incl. Argencard and Naranja X, Pago Fácil cash, installments and promotions.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Cards are 46% of e-commerce (Visa 62%, Mastercard 26%, Amex 6%, local schemes 5%) and consumers strongly prefer 'cuotas' of 3, 6, 12 or 24 months (PPRO); BCRA counts 1,866 million credit-card payments in 2025 (13.61% of retail payment count).
typical_access: direct via Payway/Fiserv, or via dLocal, EBANX, PayU

name: Naranja / Cabal
why_it_matters: Domestic schemes are 5% of card spend; Naranja has over 10 million cardholders (PPRO). dLocal and PayU accept Naranja, Cabal, Argencard and other local brands.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: E-wallets are 34% of Argentine e-commerce (PPRO), led by Mercado Pago (88 million MAU group-wide, Q2 2026).

name: Bank transfer / QR interoperable
why_it_matters: BCRA 2025: immediate push transfers were 54.53% of all retail payments by count and interoperable 'pagos con transferencia' (QR) 6.13%, i.e. 841.2 million transactions (+40.7%); bank transfer is 14% of e-commerce (PPRO).
typical_access: via dLocal (bank transfer, QR interoperable), EBANX (Debin)

name: MODO
why_it_matters: Bank-owned wallet embedded in 23 bank apps and accepting payments from 30+ banks (QR, NFC, online); no public user figure found on its site. dLocal exposes 'MODO Cards'.

name: Rapipago
why_it_matters: Cash collection network; cash is 4% of Argentine e-commerce (PPRO). Offered by dLocal and EBANX ('Cupón de Pago'). No public point count found.

name: Pago Fácil
why_it_matters: 'La primera red de cobranza de Argentina' (SEPSA); cash is 4% of e-commerce (PPRO). Offered by dLocal, EBANX and PayU. No public point count found.

name: dLocal
why_it_matters: Uruguay-born cross-border PSP (60+ countries, 1000+ methods) with full local coverage: Visa/MC/Diners/OCA/Lider cards, Abitab and RedPagos cash, online bank transfer; its market page puts single-installment credit cards at 61% of e-commerce.

name: OCA
why_it_matters: Itaú-owned card brand and acquirer (OCA Comercios) with about 30,000 merchants, processing OCA, Mastercard and Maestro and adding Visa under multi-acquiring; took 56% of Resonance (2022).

name: Fiserv
why_it_matters: Largest acquirer by merchants: more than 50,000 merchants, Mastercard's exclusive acquirer until August 2021, now multi-brand (Mastercard, Maestro, JCB, Líder, Diners, Discover, Visa).

name: Visanet
why_it_matters: Visa's acquirer in Uruguay, expected to join multi-acquiring in August 2022 when Visa opened acquiring; no newer public share figure found.

name: Getnet
why_it_matters: Santander's PagoNxt acquirer entered Uruguay (bought NAD) and works with 70+ technology integrators; no public share figure found.

name: Bamboo Payment
why_it_matters: Uruguayan PSP whose gateway docs expose RedPagos and Abitab cash coupons alongside cards; no public volume figure found.

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: Mercado Pago Connect wallet is available in Uruguay (EBANX lists Argentina, Chile, Mexico and Uruguay); no public Uruguay share figure found.

name: EBANX
why_it_matters: EBANX lists Uruguay among 'High Potential Rising Countries' with credit, debit and prepaid cards only; no local APMs confirmed.

name: Cards
why_it_matters: Credit cards dominate: 74% of online purchases in 2024 per CEDU (debit and e-wallets 26%); dLocal shows credit (1 installment) 61% and debit 7%. Installment ('cuotas') offers are standard on local cards.
typical_access: direct via OCA/Fiserv/Visanet, or via dLocal, EBANX

name: OCA
why_it_matters: Domestic card brand (Itaú) accepted at ~30,000 merchants; listed as a card option by dLocal; not reachable through cross-border acquiring, so it needs a local connection. No public share figure found.
typical_access: direct via OCA, or via dLocal

name: Mercado Pago
why_it_matters: E-wallets are 14% of Uruguayan e-commerce (dLocal); Mercado Pago Connect is available in Uruguay via EBANX. No wallet-level share figure found.

name: Bank transfer
why_it_matters: Bank transfer is 10% of Uruguayan e-commerce (dLocal); exposed as 'Online Bank Transfer' by dLocal.

name: Abitab
why_it_matters: Nationwide cash-collection network accepting e-commerce coupons (Bamboo, dLocal); cash is 4% of e-commerce (dLocal). No public point count found.

name: RedPagos
why_it_matters: Cash network with more than 450 physical locations nationwide (Bamboo docs); cash is 4% of e-commerce (dLocal).
